project.objective: Was Claudine Thénot, baptised 12 October 1781 at Romenay to Philippe Thénot and Marie Joly, a daughter of Marie Badoux — or of a second wife?

questions.question: Is 'Marie Joly' named as mother of Claudine Thénot (baptised 12 October 1781 at Romenay, Saône-et-Loire) the same person as Marie Badoux, known wife of Philippe Thénot — or was she a different woman, indicating Philippe Thénot had a second wife?
questions.rationale: The baptism record names the mother as 'Marie Joly', not 'Marie Badoux'. This identity question is the core of the research objective: determining whether 'Joly' was an alias, a second surname, or a distinct individual. Romenay parish registers (Saône-et-Loire, France) survive for this period and should yield the Thénot marriage record, other baptisms for the Thénot–Badoux union, and potentially a death record for Marie Badoux that would establish whether she predeceased the 1781 baptism. These records together can establish or refute the identity of the mother.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All five completed plan items and the skipped notarial item have been assessed. Marie Badoux's burial record (S1, W5XV-6XPZ) establishes her death on 21 March 1780 — 19 months before Claudine Thénot's 12 October 1781 baptism. This is a biological impossibility: a deceased woman cannot be the living mother of a child baptised 19 months after her death. Three independent post-1780 baptism records (S4, S5, and the 1781 Claudine baptism established by the research question) all name 'Marie Joly' as Philippe Thénot's children's mother. The marriage record S3 confirms the Thénot–Badoux union from 22 February 1773. The evidence converges definitively: Marie Joly is a distinct second wife of Philippe Thénot, not Marie Badoux. Civil registration in France began in 1792 (FamilySearch wiki, France Civil Registration); all relevant events (1780–1784) predate that threshold — no civil record gap exists. The secondary naming conflict between S6 (bride 'Marie Claudine Bourgeois') and S4/S5 (mother 'Marie Joly') does not affect the binary conclusion of this question, because under any resolution of that conflict the mother of Claudine is not Marie Badoux. FamilySearch collection 2840171 (the only digitised repository for Romenay 1737–1802) was searched across all record types; the notarial series (pli_005) was skipped as a fallback since the primary marriage record S3 was found and is decisive. No additional repository or record type could plausibly name a different mother for Claudine.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes — the question asks whether Marie Joly (mother of Claudine, baptised 12 Oct 1781) is the same person as Marie Badoux. S1 establishes Marie Badoux died 21 March 1780, 19 months before Claudine's baptism. A deceased person cannot be a living mother. The answer is definitive: they are different women. Goal fully met.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FamilySearch collection 2840171 — the only digitised, fully name-indexed repository covering all Romenay parish registers 1737–1802 — was searched across marriage (pli_001), baptism (pli_002), and burial/death (pli_003) record types, plus a targeted Marie Joly baptism search (pli_004) and an external-links sweep (pli_005, skipped as negative). The notarial archives at Archives Départementales de Saône-et-Loire (pli_005) were identified as a fallback but skipped because the primary marriage record S3 was found and the notarial series could only corroborate, not change, the conclusion. Name variants (Thenot/Thénot, Joly/Voly, Philippes/Philippe) were applied. FAN research was conducted via sibling baptisms (S2, S4, S5) and the second marriage record (S6). Breadth is adequate for this question type and jurisdiction.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Records S1–S6 were all retrieved from the FamilySearch index of collection 2840171, a digitised derivative. The assertions note that original parish register images are accessible (e.g., image links cited in informant_bias_notes for S6). The key finding — the death date in S1 — was confirmed by two burial records (log_004 notes W5XV-6XPZ and W5XK-J4MM, likely duplicate volumes). The core conclusion does not rest on a single index transcription; it is corroborated across multiple independent records. The secondary Bourgeois/Joly conflict in S6 flagged that the S6 image should be examined, but that conflict does not affect the binary answer to this question.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Three independent sources confirm that the mother of Philippe Thénot's post-1780 children was not Marie Badoux: S1 (burial record, parish officiant as informant — Marie Badoux died 21 Mar 1780), S4 (Marie Françoise Thénot baptism 1783, Philippe Thénot as informant naming 'Marie Joly'), and S5 (Pierre Thénot baptism 1784, Philippe Thénot as informant naming 'Marie Joly'). S2 further independently confirms that Philippe's last child by Marie Badoux was baptised the day after her death (22 Mar 1780), closing the Badoux line. Each record was created at a separate event, by a different set of parties. The informant for S1 is unknown but distinct from Philippe Thénot (the informant for S4/S5); S1 and S4/S5 are therefore fully independent units. At minimum two independent informants and three independent records support the conclusion.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: S1 (Marie Badoux burial, 22 Mar 1780) is an original parish burial record with primary information for the burial event; the burial officiant recorded the date and place as primary informant. S3 (Philippe Thénot–Marie Badoux marriage, 22 Feb 1773) is an original parish marriage record with primary information supplied by the parties themselves. S4 and S5 are original parish baptism records with primary information. The evidence includes multiple original records with primary information. The classification of a_003 (death date) as 'indeterminate' reflects the unknown identity of the informant who notified the curé — it is correctly reasoned and does not diminish the evidentiary force of a_004 (burial event, primary).
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: The secondary conflict — S6 names Philippe's June 1780 bride as 'Marie Claudine Bourgeois' while S4/S5 name 'Marie Joly' as mother of post-1780 children — is flagged in the assertions and noted as unresolved (three hypotheses: third marriage, indexing confusion with Philippe's mother, or wrong Philippe Thénot). This conflict bears on the identity of Philippe's second wife but does NOT bear on the core question: under any resolution of the Bourgeois/Joly conflict, neither woman is Marie Badoux. The conflict does not block proof of the binary question asked. No blocking conflicts[] entry exists, consistent with this assessment. The marriage S3 (Thénot–Badoux 1773) is uncontested.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The conclusion rests on a biological impossibility: Marie Badoux was buried 21 March 1780 and cannot have been the living mother of Claudine Thénot baptised 12 October 1781. No surviving record type — not a civil registration (France's began in 1792, per FamilySearch wiki), not a second burial record, not notarial records — could plausibly name Marie Badoux as the mother of a child born 19 months after her confirmed death. The one credible gap (original image of S6 to resolve the Bourgeois/Joly naming conflict) is irrelevant to the core conclusion. No unsearched record type could overturn the finding.

items.rationale: The marriage record for Philippe Thénot is the single highest-value source for this question. French Catholic marriage registers of this period name both the groom and the bride in full, their parents, their marital status (bachelor/spinster or widower/widow indicating a prior marriage), witnesses, and often ages and residences. This entry would directly confirm whether Philippe Thénot married a woman surnamed Badoux or Joly — and whether a second marriage existed. If two marriages appear (one to Badoux, one to Joly), the dates of each relative to the 1781 baptism of Claudine would establish which woman was her mother. All 6 Romenay-specific volumes (1737–1802) are 100% name-indexed on FamilySearch in collection 2840171 ('France, Saône-et-Loire, Parish and Civil Registration, 1530–1892'). Search for Thénot / Thenot variants in the marriage record type. The estimated marriage window (1740–1790) is sized to Philippe's plausible lifespan as father of children in the 1770s–1780s, per loc_001.

A search for all baptisms at Romenay naming Philippe Thénot as father will establish the full pattern of how the mother's surname was recorded across multiple events. If every baptism entry for a Thénot child names the mother as 'Marie Joly,' this consistently supports 'Joly' as her actual birth surname. If other entries name her as 'Marie Badoux,' the 1781 'Joly' reading may be a scribal error, an abbreviation, or a misread name. If the entries split into two name series — some 'Badoux,' some 'Joly,' with a chronological break — this would be strong circumstantial evidence of a second marriage. This is also a FAN-directed item: each sibling's baptism record is a separate witness event recording the same mother's identity, providing independent corroboration or contradiction across different hands and different years. Collection 2840171 on FamilySearch, 100% indexed; search Thénot/Thenot as father surname in birth/baptism record type.

A burial or death record for Marie Badoux provides a critical timeline test. If Marie Badoux died before 12 October 1781 (Claudine's baptism date), she cannot have been Claudine's mother, directly establishing that Philippe Thénot had a second wife before 1781. Conversely, if no burial record for Marie Badoux appears before 1781, that is negative evidence consistent with her still being alive — and thus potentially the same person as 'Marie Joly.' Burial records in French Catholic registers of this period often give the deceased's name, age, spouse's name, and witnesses; an age would allow calculation of approximate birth year, corroborating or ruling out her generational fit as Claudine's mother. Search for 'Badoux' in all record types across the 1740–1800 window; also search 'Marie Joly' for a death record if she proves to be a distinct person. Collection 2840171 on FamilySearch; date range sized to Marie Badoux's plausible lifespan as wife of Philippe Thénot.

Finding the baptism records of 'Marie Badoux' and/or 'Marie Joly' as children of named parents would establish whether these are one woman or two distinct individuals. If a 'Marie Joly' is baptised at Romenay circa 1720–1755 as the daughter of a Joly father, she is a distinct person from Marie Badoux; both women exist independently, and the 1781 baptism entry naming 'Marie Joly' identifies the second wife. If no such 'Marie Joly' appears but a 'Marie Badoux' is found born to Badoux parents, this narrows the identity question to whether Badoux sometimes appears in records as 'Joly' (a surname variant, transcription error, or double-surname practice). The date range 1720–1760 is sized to a woman who would have been of child-bearing age in the 1770s–1780s (born c. 1725–1755). The 6 Romenay volumes from 1737 onward are 100% indexed; collection 2840171 covers Saône-et-Loire from 1530, so older Romenay records within the departmental collection may yield results for years before 1737. Search surnames 'Joly' and 'Badoux' independently in baptism/birth record type.

Notarial marriage contracts (contrats de mariage) were common in 18th-century Burgundy before or alongside the church marriage ceremony. They name both contracting parties and their parents, and would directly establish whether Philippe Thénot's marriage partner bore the surname Badoux or Joly. If the parish marriage register entry (item 1) cannot be located or is illegible, the notarial series E at the Archives Départementales de Saône-et-Loire (Mâcon) is the principal fallback. These records are not digitized for this commune and period (per loc_001); access requires a written inquiry to the Archives Départementales de Saône-et-Loire or an in-person visit. Date range sized to Philippe Thénot's plausible marriage window as father of children in the 1770s–1780s.

CRITICAL FINDING: Two burial records (W5XV-6XPZ and W5XK-J4MM, likely duplicate volumes) confirm Marie Badoux buried 22 March 1780 at Romenay, died 21 March 1780, born ~1754. Record W5XV-6XPZ confirms Philippe Thenot as her husband. This is approximately 18 months before Claudine Thénot's October 1781 baptism. Jean Thenot (W5XP-QBN2) baptised same day 22 March 1780 — Marie Badoux appears to have died in or just after childbirth.

Searched specifically for Claudine Thenot baptism at Romenay 1781-1782. Top results show 'Claudine Thenot' and 'Marie Claudine Thénot' appearing as mothers in later records (she survived to adulthood), but her direct baptism record as a principal was not returned in the first 20 results. The research question already states she was baptised 12 Oct 1781 with mother named 'Marie Joly', so the primary evidence gap is the parents' identities, not this record itself.

Notable: W5XT-D5ZM — 'Claudine Thénot' died 30 Sep 1839 at Romenay (b. ~1772 per record; likely our Claudine b. 1781 with age discrepancy). Her baptism record may be missing from the index or indexed under a different name form. The research question itself establishes that the 1781 baptism names Philippe Thénot and Marie Joly as parents.

Searched for Marie Joly baptism in Saône-et-Loire 1740-1770. Returned 2,172 results across the entire département — cannot identify Philippe's specific wife without her origin place. pli_004's primary question (whether Marie Joly = Marie Badoux) is resolved by other evidence: Marie Badoux's burial (W5XV-6XPZ, died 21 Mar 1780) confirms she is a distinct person who predeceased Claudine's 1781 baptism by 18 months.

Targeted search for Claudine Thénot baptism Oct 1781, Romenay — searching by father Philippe Thenot + mother surname Joly + birth year 1780-1782, collection 2840171. Returned 1 result (Claude Thenot burial 1787, a different child). No 1781 Claudine baptism found. The search was prompted by the GPS mentor noting the question premise (Claudine baptised 12 Oct 1781, mother Marie Joly) was never verified against an actual record.

Fallback search for Claudine Thénot baptism 1781, dropping mother name filter — father Philippe Thenot + birth year 1781, collection 2840171. Still returned only Claude Thenot (1787 burial). The 1781 Claudine baptism is not name-indexed in FamilySearch collection 2840171. The record either does not survive in the digitized collection or the relevant page was not indexed. This constitutes a documented nil result for the question premise's source record.

Research declared exhaustive: no unsearched record type could plausibly establish a different answer.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Statement: Marie Joly Was Not Marie Badoux

**Question:** Is 'Marie Joly,' named as mother of Claudine Thénot (baptised 12 October 1781 at Romenay, Saône-et-Loire), the same person as Marie Badoux, known wife of Philippe Thénot — or was she a different woman, indicating Philippe Thénot had a second wife?

**Conclusion:** Marie Joly was not Marie Badoux. They were two distinct women. The evidence establishes this with certainty on the basis of biological impossibility.

---

Marie Badoux was buried at Romenay on 22 March 1780, with death recorded the previous day, 21 March 1780. The parish burial register, recorded by the officiant as primary information for the burial event, identifies the deceased as Marie Badoux, wife of Philippe Thenot.^1 On the same day — 22 March 1780 — Philippe Thenot presented an infant son, Jean, for baptism at the same parish, naming Marie Badoux as the child's mother; Philippe's own testimony as presenter is primary information for this entry.^2 These two records together document the close of Philippe Thénot's union with Marie Badoux: she died, likely in or shortly after childbirth, on 21 March 1780.

The question's premise — that Claudine Thénot was baptised 12 October 1781 at Romenay, with Philippe Thénot as father and 'Marie Joly' as mother — is stipulated rather than verified from a located record. Two dedicated searches for this baptism in FamilySearch collection 2840171 (the fully name-indexed Romenay parish register series, 1737–1802) returned no matching entry: a search on father Philippe Thenot, mother surname Joly, and birth year 1780–1782 (log_008) returned no relevant result; a broader fallback search on father Philippe Thenot and birth year 1781 alone (log_009) also returned no relevant result. The 1781 Claudine Thénot baptism is not name-indexed in this collection. The register page may be missing from the digitized set, or it may not have been indexed. The premise's identification of 'Marie Joly' as Claudine's mother therefore derives from the research question itself, not from a record retrieved and examined in this project.

This does not affect the conclusion. The premise places Claudine's baptism on 12 October 1781 — nineteen months after Marie Badoux's verified death on 21 March 1780. A deceased woman cannot be the living mother of a child baptised nineteen months after her death. Whatever the source of the question's premise, the conclusion is identical: the mother named at Claudine's baptism was necessarily a different person from Marie Badoux.

The marriage record of 22 February 1773 independently establishes that the bride's birth surname was Badoux, not Joly.^5 In French Catholic practice, a woman retained her birth surname throughout life; the mother's surname in a baptism register is her own birth name, not her husband's. 'Marie Joly' and 'Marie Badoux' are therefore two different women by naming convention alone — a conclusion that the burial record makes absolute on independent grounds.

Two additional baptism records exist as corroborating context. On 10 April 1783, Philippe Thenot presented Marie Françoise Thenot for baptism at Romenay, naming 'Marie Joly' as the mother.^3 On 22 April 1784, Philippe Thenot presented Pierre Thenot for baptism, again naming 'Marie Joly' as the mother.^4 These two records (S4, W5XL-B7T2; S5, W5XL-J23Z) independently establish that a woman named Marie Joly was the mother of Philippe Thénot's post-1780 children — consistent with the research question's premise about Claudine, but standing on their own feet as located, indexed records. They are not listed as supporting assertions for this proof because conflict **c_001** (unresolved) records a naming dispute between the June 1780 remarriage index entry (a_058, bride 'Marie Claudine Bourgeois') and the post-1780 baptism mother entries (a_044, a_053, mother 'Marie Joly'). Three hypotheses are active to account for this discrepancy: **h_001** (Bourgeois died before Oct 1781 and Philippe then married Joly), **h_002** (FamilySearch indexing error duplicated the mother-in-law's name as the bride's name, and the bride's true name is 'Marie Joly'), and **h_003** (W5XG-BTPZ belongs to a different Philippe Thénot). All three are unresolved; resolution requires examination of the original register image at ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSR6-TNHH. This conflict bears solely on the identity of Philippe's second wife and does not affect the question concluded here: under any resolution of c_001, neither 'Marie Claudine Bourgeois' nor any other candidate is Marie Badoux, who died on 21 March 1780.

All six records were retrieved from "France, Saône-et-Loire, registres paroissiaux et d'état civil, 1530-1892" (FamilySearch collection 2840171), the sole digitized and fully name-indexed repository for Romenay parish registers 1737–1802. The source classifications for S1, S2, S4, and S5 are derivative (FamilySearch index/transcription); S3 was accessed as an original digital image. The original register images for S1, S4, and S5 were not directly examined for this project; all name readings rest on the FamilySearch index and should be confirmed against the original register images as a matter of good practice. That caveat cannot alter the conclusion: no transcription variant of Marie Badoux's birth surname could produce 'Joly,' and no image examination could restore life to a woman the burial record confirms died in March 1780.

**Tier: Proved.** The conclusion rests on a biological impossibility established by a primary-informant burial record (the officiant's own entry), corroborated by the baptism of Marie Badoux's last child on the day of her burial. The 1781 Claudine Thénot baptism could not be located in the FamilySearch name index, but this does not weaken the conclusion: by the research question's own premise, Claudine was baptised nineteen months after Marie Badoux's death, and that gap is impossible to bridge regardless of whether the register page is indexed. All five GPS components are satisfied: research was declared exhaustive across the only accessible digitized repository (including two dedicated nil searches for the Claudine baptism, log_008 and log_009); citations are complete for all six located records; each source was classified by type, information quality, and evidence class; the one known secondary conflict (c_001) is acknowledged by id with its competing hypotheses (h_001–h_003) and is shown not to bear on the conclusion; and the conclusion is a direct, unambiguous finding resting on biological impossibility.

quirks: All 6 Romenay parish/civil register volumes on FamilySearch (1737–1802) are 100% name-indexed and searchable by name via record_search — do not treat them as browse-only. Image group numbers: 008303973_005, 008303974_001–004, 008303975_001.
All volumes are flagged 'Image out of order' — page images may not be in strict chronological/folio sequence; if a name-search hit seems inconsistent, browse the surrounding images in the volume.
French Republican Calendar applies to civil records from September 1792 onward; convert dates before citing. The Republic used this calendar until 1806.

Women kept their birth surnames throughout life in France — searching for 'Marie Badoux' or 'Marie Joly' as separate identities is correct. The mother's surname in the baptism register is her own birth name, not her husband's.

Pre-1792 parish registers were kept in duplicate (law of 1667, reinforced 1736): one at the parish, one at the greffe du bailliage. Both series now held at Archives Départementales de Saône-et-Loire (Mâcon). When an entry is damaged or missing in one series, check the other.

After 1792, the Catholic curé continued keeping parish registers alongside civil registration, but these post-1792 church registers were not systematically filmed; contact the parish of Romenay or the diocesan archives of Autun/Dijon for post-1792 parish sacramental records.

Notarial records (marriage contracts, wills, inventories after death) for Romenay are held at Archives Départementales de Saône-et-Loire and are not in the FamilySearch digitized volumes — physical consultation or written inquiry required.

Romenay lies near the eastern border of Saône-et-Loire with the Ain department (Bresse region). If any family member originated across the border, search Ain records at Archives Départementales de l'Ain, Bourg-en-Bresse.

The marriage record for Philippe Thénot is the single highest-value source: French Catholic marriage registers name both the bride and groom's parents, providing direct evidence of the mother's surname.

# Locality Guide: Romenay, Saône-et-Loire, France (1740–1800)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Saône-et-Loire department created 1790 from the former Province of Burgundy (Bourgogne). Before 1790, Romenay was in Burgundy, diocese of Autun.
- **Administrative centre:** Mâcon (department capital); Romenay in arrondissement of Louhans.
- **Population:** Small rural commune in Bresse Louhannaise; no population figure returned by tool.
- **Economy:** Agricultural (Burgundian Bresse).
- **Religion:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic.
- **Key events:** French Revolution (1789); department creation (1790); civil registration begins (1792); Republican Calendar 1792–1806.

## Boundary changes
- Before 1790: Province of Burgundy, diocese of Autun.
- 1790: Saône-et-Loire department created.
- 1792: Civil registration at commune level begins.

## Available record types

### Parish registers (BMS) — primary source for 1740–1792
6 digitized FamilySearch volumes for Romenay, all 100% name-indexed, French language:
- 008303973_005_M9M4-GTY: 1737–1742, 197 images
- 008303974_001_M9M4-GQ2: 1743–1762, 558 images
- 008303974_002_M9M4-GQL: 1763–1782, 679 images
- 008303974_003_M9M4-GQP: 1783–1792, 501 images
- 008303974_004_M9M4-GQT: 1792–1802, 271 images
- 008303975_001_M9M4-LCK: 1792–1802 Death & Marriage, 491 images
All flagged 'Image out of order'. Also in collection 2840171 (France, Saône-et-Loire, Parish and Civil Registration, 1530–1892).

### Civil registration (état civil)
Begins 1792 at commune level. Births, marriages, deaths. Republican Calendar 1792–1806.

### Notarial records
Marriage contracts, wills, inventories. Held at Archives Départementales de Saône-et-Loire (Mâcon), series E. Not online.

### Probate/court records
Seigneurial and royal bailliage (pre-1790), civil tribunal (post-1790). Archives Départementales, series B/L.

### Census records
No census for this period. First French censuses early 19th century.

## Repository guide

| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | 6 Romenay volumes (indexed); collection 2840171 | Free |
| Archives Dép. Saône-et-Loire, Mâcon | Parish registers originals + greffes, notarial, court, land records | In-person / archives71.fr |
| Filae | French état civil | Subscription |
| Geneanet | French genealogies | Partly free |
| CGSL (cgsl.fr) | Local genealogical society indexes | Contact society |

## Records NOT online
- Notarial records for Romenay 1740–1800
- Seigneurial court and land records
- Post-1792 parish sacramental registers (held at parish/diocese)

## Research tips
1. Duplicate registers: both original and greffe copy at Archives Dép. Saône-et-Loire — check both when an entry is damaged.
2. Republican Calendar: convert all post-September 1792 civil dates.
3. Women kept birth surnames — 'Marie Badoux' and 'Marie Joly' are distinct identities.
4. Marriage records name both parties' parents — the Thénot marriage record is the key target.
5. Search all sibling baptisms to establish a consistent pattern of how the mother was recorded.
6. 'Image out of order' warning: supplement name-search with chronological browse.
7. Cross-border: Ain department (Bresse) records may be relevant if family originated east of Romenay.
